paragraphs: Here's what jumps out at me, friend. Joab does the hard work. He fights, he captures the royal fortress, he takes the water supply (2 Samuel 12:26-27). Then he sends word to David to come finish it, because otherwise the city "will be named after me" (2 Samuel 12:28). I think Joab knew exactly whose name belonged on that victory, and he gave the credit away.

Now look at what David does. When Joab sends word, David assembles all the troops, goes to Rabbah, fights against it and captures it (2 Samuel 12:29). Then the crown is placed on David's head, and he takes a great amount of plunder (2 Samuel 12:30). This win came in two parts, Joab's work first and then David's finish.

So here's the big idea. Big jobs take more than one set of hands, and in this passage Joab and David each do their part to take Rabbah. The end of the passage is heavy, because David puts the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks and axes (2 Samuel 12:31). Today, look at who is working beside you on your big jobs, and be ready to do your part when the call comes, like David when Joab sent word.
